description: Availability Bias Correction: Cetaceans spend time underwater and may not be visible when the survey passes over them, leading to underestimation.Availability Correction applies dive-time models to adjust for the proportion of time cetaceans are underwater and not visible to observers. Data from tagging studies or direct observations inform these corrections.

Detection Bias (Perception Bias) Correction: Some animals are missed even if they are within the survey area due to observer fatigue, poor weather conditions, or animals being underwater at the moment of observation. Detection Probability Correction  uses distance sampling (e.g., line-transect surveys) to estimate the probability of detecting an animal at different distances from the survey track. A detection function is fitted to correct for missed individuals. Observer Bias Correction uses double-platform surveys (independent observer teams) to estimate how often one team detects animals that the other team misses. This helps quantify perception bias.
Group Size Estimation Correction: Adjusts for errors in estimating group sizes, often using photographic evidence or post-survey validation.

Survey Coverage Bias: Some areas may be unsurveyed due to logistical constraints, leading to gaps in data. Coverage Probability Adjustment: If some regions are unsurveyed, statistical models (e.g., spatial modeling) interpolate data to estimate abundance in those areas.

Responsive Movement Bias: Some species may avoid or be attracted to survey vessels or aircraft, affecting counts. Responsive Movement Correction: Analyzes behavioral responses to survey platforms (e.g., bow-riding dolphins or diving whales) to correct for attraction or avoidance effects.
